cases.diagnosis: Probable MRSA coronary stent infection causing an infected coronary pseudoaneurysm with stent disruption and associated purulent pericarditis, producing cardiac tamponade and shock.

Atrial standstill with complete atrioventricular block and a slow junctional escape rhythm, causing symptomatic bradycardia and contributing to predominantly right-sided heart failure; the underlying atrial disease remains unconfirmed.
Intraperitoneal rupture of a MAINZ urinary pouch with urinary leakage into the peritoneum, most likely precipitated by impaired catheter drainage and reservoir overdistension.
Biopsy-confirmed extensive-stage small cell lung carcinoma with recurrent cancer-associated right pleural effusion and severe right-middle-lobe bronchial narrowing contributing to dyspnea.
Malignant melanoma involving the left pleura, with an unidentified primary site, causing a malignant pleural effusion and contributing to hypoxemic respiratory failure.
Primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease) caused by bilateral tuberculous adrenalitis with granulomatous adrenal destruction.
Pembrolizumab-associated autoimmune hemolytic anemia causing profound anemia and predominantly unconjugated jaundice.

Spontaneous cervicothoracic spinal epidural hematoma extending from C6 to T2, causing acute spinal cord compression with paraplegia and sphincter dysfunction; the underlying bleeding source is undetermined.
Ileal perforation caused by a migrated biliary stent lodged in a Meckel diverticulum, with purulent peritonitis.
Omental abdominal ectopic pregnancy between the spleen and descending colon, with active hemorrhage causing hemoperitoneum.

cases.diagnosis: Probable MRSA infection of the coronary stent and adjacent arterial wall, causing an infected coronary pseudoaneurysm with stent disruption and associated pericardial tamponade.
unconfirmed: MRSA infection of the coronary stent and arterial wall
Pseudoaneurysm rupture or pericardial communication
Bacterial infection of the pericardial fluid
Myocardial infarction or specific mechanism of regional ventricular dysfunction
Persistent bacteremia or concomitant endocarditis
next_steps: Emergency cardiothoracic surgical management of the expanding pseudoaneurysm and disrupted stent, with ongoing shock and tamponade support.
Obtain operative assessment and coronary arterial/stent specimens for culture and histopathology; culture pericardial fluid if available.
Verify current antimicrobial treatment and ensure appropriate intravenous MRSA therapy with infectious-disease input.
Obtain follow-up blood cultures to document clearance and repeat echocardiography to assess effusion, ventricular function, and possible endocarditis.

cases.diagnosis: Probable atrial-predominant myocarditis, most likely postinfectious, causing extensive atrial electrical standstill and complete atrioventricular block.
unconfirmed: Postinfectious cause and specific pathogen
Histological myocarditis and inflammatory subtype
Mesalazine causality
Previous rhythm status and chronicity of atrial disease
Cause of pulmonary pressure elevation, RV dysfunction and severe tricuspid regurgitation
Electrolyte and thyroid abnormalities; requested results were unavailable
next_steps: Urgent monitored cardiology assessment for complete AV block, pacing and treatment of congestion.
Establish mesalazine initiation and dose-change dates; jointly review possible withdrawal or substitution with cardiology and gastroenterology.
Retrieve prior ECGs and imaging; obtain electrolytes, renal function and thyroid testing.
Consider targeted atrial biopsy with histopathology at an experienced center if feasible and management-changing; use serial imaging and rhythm assessment to evaluate evolution.
Reassess right-sided dysfunction, tricuspid regurgitation and pulmonary pressures after stabilization; investigate persistent abnormalities.

cases.diagnosis: Probable drainage-failure–related overdistension and rupture of a MAINZ urinary pouch, causing intraperitoneal urinary leakage.
unconfirmed: Catheter obstruction and pressure-related pouch overdistension as the initiating mechanism
Traumatic, ischemic, or other structural contributors to rupture
Bacterial peritonitis or septic shock
next_steps: Review operative details and prior reconstruction records for tissue viability, defect characteristics, catheter position, and evidence of obstruction or trauma.
Maintain and verify unobstructed pouch drainage with urology follow-up; monitor urine output, renal function, and cardiopulmonary recovery.
If infection remains suspected, obtain appropriate cultures and reassess clinically; use follow-up pouch contrast imaging as clinically indicated to assess repair integrity.

cases.diagnosis: Small cell lung carcinoma–associated chylothorax, most likely from malignant obstruction of thoracic lymphatic drainage.
unconfirmed: Exact site and anatomical mechanism of malignant lymphatic obstruction or leakage
Direct pleural malignant involvement
Potential contributions from surgery, trauma or medications
next_steps: Promptly reassess respiratory status and manage symptomatic recurrent fluid.
Coordinate oncology and pleural specialist care for biopsy-confirmed small cell carcinoma and chylothorax, including nutritional assessment.
Review the actual CT report and complete surgery, trauma and medication histories.
Obtain lymphatic imaging when available if persistent leakage or intervention planning requires localization; reassess the mechanism if imaging identifies another cause.

cases.diagnosis: Melanoma involving the left pleura, most likely metastatic from an unidentified primary, causing a malignant pleural effusion.
unconfirmed: Primary melanoma site and full disease extent
Metastatic origin versus rare primary pleural melanoma
Whether the pleural disease fully explains hypoxemia and crackles
Pulmonary embolism exclusion
next_steps: Obtain integrated pathology review of pleural tissue morphology and immunostains to finalize classification.
Arrange oncology assessment, staging, and further primary-site evaluation.
Continue oxygen and reassess respiratory status and residual effusion after the documented thoracentesis.
If hypoxemia remains unexplained, assess additional pulmonary causes and obtain dedicated embolism testing as clinically indicated.

cases.diagnosis: Tuberculous adrenalitis causing primary adrenal insufficiency.
unconfirmed: Viable organisms and tuberculosis drug susceptibility; mycobacterial culture unavailable
Current extra-adrenal tuberculosis activity
Timed morning cortisol and dynamic adrenal testing
Mineralocorticoid deficiency and current hemodynamic stability
Fungal culture unavailable
next_steps: Promptly assess blood pressure, orthostasis, hydration, glucose, electrolytes, and adrenal-crisis symptoms; treat suspected crisis immediately with hydrocortisone and IV saline.
Arrange endocrinology management of glucocorticoid replacement; assess renin and aldosterone to guide mineralocorticoid replacement.
Obtain infectious-disease or tuberculosis-service assessment for antituberculous treatment, susceptibility testing where feasible, and evaluation for active pulmonary disease.
Coordinate replacement dosing during tuberculosis therapy because rifampicin increases glucocorticoid clearance; provide stress-dosing and emergency steroid education.

cases.diagnosis: Pembrolizumab-associated autoimmune hemolytic anemia, a probable immune-related adverse reaction.
unconfirmed: Causal attribution to pembrolizumab
Warm versus mixed or cold antibody subtype
Prior autoimmune hemolysis or recent transfusion
Concurrent gastrointestinal bleeding
Other medication or malignancy-associated triggers
next_steps: Immediate hospital admission and hematology assessment; urgent transfusion support coordinated with the blood bank for symptomatic hemoglobin 45 g/L.
Withhold pembrolizumab and initiate specialist-directed treatment for severe immune hemolysis, typically corticosteroids.
Complete antibody characterization, including monospecific DAT review, antibody screen/elution and the pending cold agglutinin titer; assess thermal amplitude if indicated.
Retrieve baseline blood counts, oncology records, medication and transfusion history; monitor hemoglobin and hemolysis markers to assess response.
Evaluate dark stools for concurrent bleeding and obtain liver enzymes and coagulation studies to assess additional pathology.

cases.diagnosis: Spontaneous cervicothoracic spinal epidural hemorrhage causing acute compressive myelopathy; the underlying bleeding source remains undetermined.
unconfirmed: Specific bleeding source or precipitant
Absence of previous spinal procedures
Personal or familial bleeding tendency despite normal screening coagulation tests
Occult spinal vascular abnormality
Exact onset and rate of motor deterioration
next_steps: Immediate spinal surgical assessment for emergency decompression and hematoma evacuation.
Serial neurological examinations and supportive management of paralysis and sphincter dysfunction.
Clarify procedure and bleeding histories without delaying treatment.

Use operative findings and specialist-directed follow-up imaging, with vascular investigation if indicated, to evaluate the bleeding source; pursue additional hemostatic testing if history or recurrent bleeding warrants it.

cases.diagnosis: Migrated biliary stent lodged in a Meckel diverticulum, causing adjacent ileal perforation and purulent peritonitis.
unconfirmed: Prior biliary stent placement, indication, timing, and migration route
Definitive mechanical obstruction and contribution of adhesions
Systemic infection severity and bowel viability beyond the reported perforation
next_steps: Ensure operative source control, including stent removal and appropriate treatment of the perforated ileum and Meckel diverticulum; completion was not reported.
Provide resuscitation, intravenous antibiotics, and postoperative monitoring for sepsis and complications.
Review biliary procedure records to establish stent origin and assess any remaining biliary management needs.

cases.diagnosis: Bleeding abdominal ectopic pregnancy involving the omentum, most likely an omental implantation.
unconfirmed: Primary versus secondary abdominal implantation
Precise microscopic implantation site within the omentum
Complete removal and subsequent resolution of gestational tissue
next_steps: Ensure surgical hemostasis and monitor vital signs and hemoglobin after documented intra-abdominal bleeding.
Follow serial quantitative hCG to resolution to assess for persistent gestational tissue.
Review the operative and detailed pathology reports to clarify implantation site and completeness of removal.

cases.diagnosis: Probable atrial-predominant inflammatory cardiomyopathy (atrial myocarditis), provisionally postinfectious, causing extensive atrial electrical failure and complete atrioventricular block.
unconfirmed: Postinfectious etiology and specific infectious agent
Histologic atrial myocarditis, including giant-cell or eosinophilic subtypes
Mesalazine causality and relationship to ulcerative colitis
Thyroid, electrolyte, and renal contributors
Cause and persistence of elevated pulmonary pressure and RV dysfunction
next_steps: Urgent monitored cardiology care and pacing assessment for complete AV block; assess hemodynamic stability and treat congestion.
Establish mesalazine initiation/dose chronology and colitis activity; coordinate medication review with cardiology and gastroenterology.
Obtain potassium, renal function, thyroid tests, and blood count; follow troponin and cardiac function.
Consider targeted atrial biopsy with histology if feasible and management-changing; repeat cardiac imaging to assess inflammatory evolution.
Reassess RV function, tricuspid regurgitation, and pulmonary pressure after stabilization; investigate persistent pulmonary hypertension.

cases.diagnosis: Likely pressure-related rupture of a MAINZ urinary pouch following catheter drainage failure, with intraperitoneal urinary leakage.
unconfirmed: Catheter obstruction and consequent pouch overdistension as the rupture mechanism
Recent catheter manipulation or direct traumatic injury
Tissue ischemia, necrosis, recurrent malignancy, or infection contributing to rupture
Exact cause and severity of cardiopulmonary decompensation
next_steps: Review catheter patency, position, drainage records, and any preceding manipulation to assess the proposed obstructive mechanism.
Obtain detailed operative findings concerning rupture margins and evidence of trauma, necrosis, or structural disease; review histology if tissue was sampled.
Continue postoperative surgical and urological monitoring of pouch drainage, abdominal findings, respiratory and circulatory status, urine output, and renal function.
Arrange urological follow-up to establish reliable long-term pouch emptying and prevent recurrent retention.

cases.diagnosis: Small cell lung carcinoma–associated recurrent right pleural effusion, with suspected tumor-related impairment of pleural lymphatic drainage and contribution from bronchial obstruction.
unconfirmed: Direct malignant involvement of the pleura
Exact mechanism and biochemical classification of the effusion
Cause of pulmonary infiltrates
Pulmonary embolism and cardiac contribution have not been excluded
next_steps: Prompt oncology and pulmonary assessment for confirmed extensive-stage small cell lung carcinoma.
Reassess respiratory status and effusion size; arrange therapeutic drainage if clinically indicated.
If distinguishing pleural involvement would change management, obtain repeat cytology and consider pleural biopsy; obtain paired serum studies for effusion classification.
Assess persistent or disproportionate dyspnea for additional causes, including embolism or cardiac disease, as clinically indicated.

cases.diagnosis: Pleural involvement by melanoma with an unidentified primary site, causing a malignant left pleural effusion.
unconfirmed: Pleural tissue histology confirming melanoma
Primary melanoma site and disease extent
Relative contributions to hypoxemia; concomitant embolism, infection or cardiac disease
next_steps: Continue hospital oxygen support and monitor respiratory status.
Obtain urgent oncology assessment and expert review of pleural cytology/immunohistochemistry; pursue targeted pleural biopsy when available.
Stage suspected melanoma and complete a directed search for an occult primary.
Assess residual or recurrent effusion for therapeutic drainage; investigate persistent disproportionate hypoxemia, including whether diagnostic pulmonary angiography is needed.

cases.diagnosis: Bilateral tuberculous adrenalitis causing primary adrenal insufficiency, strongly supported by detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA in adrenal biopsy tissue.
unconfirmed: Mycobacterial viability and drug susceptibility
Duration and extent of active tuberculosis
Cosyntropin response and cortisol sampling times
Mineralocorticoid deficiency and current hemodynamic status
Fungal culture result; testing was queued, not performed
next_steps: Promptly assess blood pressure, orthostasis, hydration, glucose, electrolytes, and adrenal crisis symptoms; treat immediately if crisis is suspected.
Arrange endocrinology care for glucocorticoid replacement and assessment of mineralocorticoid replacement needs.
Arrange tuberculosis specialist care for treatment, evaluation of other involved sites, and resistance testing or culture if obtainable.
If clinically necessary and safe, clarify adrenal reserve with documented paired morning cortisol/ACTH or cosyntropin testing without delaying needed treatment.

Assess dark stools for bleeding and obtain missing liver enzymes, pursuing endoscopy or biliary imaging as clinically indicated.

interpretation: Original and prospective runs are distinct encounters; offline review reuses original evidence and adds no encounter.
Working etiological hypothesis may be unconfirmed; judge agreement does not establish confirmation, clinical accuracy, safety or superiority.
Ten shared selected public cases and one encounter per arm do not establish ConsistencyDx or a generalizable performance estimate.
Self-reported confidence is not a validated clinical probability.
Token sums include durable answered responses only; interrupted subscription calls with unknown usage make totals lower bounds.
Cached input is part of input tokens and must not be added to input totals again.
token_quantile_method: linear interpolation at (n-1)*p; distributions use per-case sums, not pooled per-request counts
